children: TECH SELLS OFF AFTER ANTHROPIC CEO COMMENTS; 10-YEAR YIELD ABOVE 5%

Major U.S. stock indexes are down in early trading Monday, with chipmakers and other technology shares selling off after Anthropic's CEO urged AI companies to slow development, and as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield
is down 4.9% while the S&P 500 technology index
is off 1.7%. Shares of top chipmaker Nvidia

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Saturday called on AI companies to slow the pace at which they advance model capabilities. Elon Musk, who runs xAI, and ​OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said they agreed with Amodei.
Chipmakers have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI spending boom. Even with the day's declines, the chipmaker index remains up nearly 60% YTD.

Investors are also on edge ahead of this week's Federal Reserve announcement, with last week's consumer price data driving up expectations for an interest rate hike from the U.S. central bank. The 10-year benchmark Treasury yield rose above 5% on Monday for the first time since October 2023. Traders now are pricing in a roughly 90% chance of a rate increase by the Fed, according to CME's FedWatch.
Main US indexes decline; Nasdaq down >1%
Tech is weakest S&P 500 sector; consumer staples up the most
Dollar rallies >0.5%; bitcoin gains >1%; US crude advances >3.5%; gold down >1.5%
